# Location

## Summary
A named physical place — somewhere things happen, ship to, or are held at.
Shared-realm block at `location.gts`.

## API
- `name` — StringField (drives `cardTitle`)
- `kind` — StringField label in the consumer's vocabulary (Stadium, Office, Warehouse); deliberately free text and never a lifecycle, so it is not colour-coded
- `address` — base `AddressField`
- `geo` — catalog `GeoPointField` (`{ lat, lon }`); shown as text latitude/longitude only, no map
- `phone` — base `PhoneNumberField`; `website` — base `WebsiteField`
- `description` — MarkdownField

## Usage
```ts
import { Location } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/events/location';

@field venue = linksTo(Location);
```
Embedded is a card with a header (pin mark, name, ancestor path), a kind
pill, the city/country line and a key-value list (kind, parent, street,
phone); fitted adds place, kind and ancestor path progressively across the
size tiers; isolated is the place's page: a stat strip (depth, kind, city),
then Path, Address and About on the left, and Linked and Details (kind,
parent, city, phone, website, geo) on the right.

## Nesting
Places nest through `parent`: a room is in a floor, in a building, on a site.
`parentName` and `pathLabel` ("Building B › Floor 2") are one-hop labels a
fitted view can show without resolving links; a consumer that needs the full
path walks `parent`, as the Location Tree does.

## Non-goals
Everything a place means to one domain stays on the consumer: a stadium's
capacity (see the Capacity field), a warehouse's racking, an office's desks.
That split is what lets one Location serve an event's venue and an order's
pickup point without either seeing the other's baggage.
